column28: Ensuring that students and those teaching understand how LLMs/ generative AI works, what it can and cannot do and therefore to be able to make informed decisions about whether to use it and know how to make any use as safe as possible. The use of AI massively increases the workload for instructors. My own experience is of extremely poor quality responses that don't answer the assessment requirements and therefore necessitate a lot of time consuming feedback or issues around documenting issues. It also means changing assessments to limit "cheating" which is sometimes very frustrating as you want to pick assessments that are also pedagogically useful for the students' learning rather than for their robustness against llm use. On top of that, it adds an extra need to discuss AI within already packed programs. We are being forced to react to a technology in ways that impact on the time we have to teach what the courses are actually about. This is terribly detrimental to learners and teachers.
